One task per page: the goal, the steps in the app, the same thing from the command line. New to Gen Studio? Start with the tutorials.

Make more takes and keep the best: retake a step, compare takes side by side, choose the one in use. Replace a take with a new roll: a new seed in the same place, the old pictures kept. Rebuild the stale steps: bring an asset up to date after you change a take. Add, branch, skip and delete steps: the next step, another route from any step, and taking one away. Write a prompt the model understands: the writing helper, the prompt guide, saved prompts and presets. Watch, pause and cancel jobs: what's running, what's waiting, and what to do when a job fails.
Repaint part of a picture: mark an area by hand and redraw only that. Change one part of a concept by naming it: no mask to draw, one new take.

Repaint a model's texture: a new texture from a picture, baked onto the same mesh. Change one part of a 3D model: mark it in the viewer, then repaint, replace or attach. Make hair, capes and skirts swing: bone chains that Godot simulates. Bring in a model you already have: FBX, OBJ, GLB, VRM or .blend as a prop or character.

Layer a sound and add effects: the mixer on the Effects step. Clean up a sound or track: rumble, clicks, hiss, shimmer and a dull top end. Edit a composed piece bar by bar: new ideas for a bar or one instrument, your own notes, saved as a new take. Split a track into stems and edit its MIDI: Stems, MIDI and the MIDI editor.
Export an asset to Godot: what lands in your project, and where. Import from inside the Godot editor: the Gen Studio dock.
Run many jobs overnight: a batch file with jobs and a matrix. Watch the queue from your phone: takes, progress, pause and batches on a page on your network.

Find and import free assets: models, textures, sounds, music, shaders and voices, with their licences. Move the data folder to another disk: and see what uses the space. Keep models on the drive you choose: library folders, per extension.

Turn extensions on and off: which packs of steps and models you have. Run a step with a Kit: an optional recipe for a step, picked by a picture card. Write an extension: your own step, with a manifest and a worker.
You get many assets made from one file while you're away. A batch runs at low priority, behind anything you queue by hand.
A project: a folder with gen-project.toml. The models for the steps you'll run (gen install weights). A step whose model isn't installed is refused up front.

Make a batches/ folder in the project and write a file in it, say batches/overnight.yaml: jobs: # plain jobs, as in a job file - {asset: lantern, kind: prop, prompt: a brass alchemist's lantern with blue glass panes, seed: 1} - {asset: courier, kind: character, prompt: a young courier with short auburn hair} matrix: # every combination of the list-valued fields kind: prop <Term tip="One thing you make, such as a prop, a character, a sound or a texture, kept as a folder in the project's assets folder." to="/docs/glossary/#asset">asset</Term>: "{prompt}_{seed}" # a name pattern prompt: [a wooden chair, a stone well, an iron lantern] <Term tip="The number that fixes a model's random choices, so the same seed with the same settings gives the same result." to="/docs/glossary/#seed">seed</Term>: [1, 2] <Term tip="How long a step may take (Ultra fast, Fast, Balanced or Quality), which picks the model and its settings." to="/docs/glossary/#profile">profile</Term>: [balanced] Run it from the project folder: gen batch batches/overnight.yaml Leave it. gen batch works through the queue and reports each step as it finishes. The whole file is checked first: if one job is wrong, nothing is queued.

The matrix: A matrix needs kind and an asset name pattern. Each field with a list is varied. Fields with one value are the same for every job. The example makes 3 prompts × 2 seeds = 6 props. In the pattern, {n} counts from 1, and {prompt}, {seed}, {profile} or any other field are short slugs of the value. "{prompt}_{seed}" gives a_wooden_chair_1, a_stone_well_2 and so on. Two jobs can't make the same asset name. Make the pattern include every varied field, or use {n}. Any other key goes to the steps' forms, as in a job file (slot: for a wearable, bpm: for music). The keys are in Files and steps and fields. How it runs: Jobs that use the same model run one after another, so the model isn't reloaded between them. If the machine crashes or you stop it, the job that was cut off goes back in the queue. gen queue run picks up where it stopped. Running gen batch again would queue the whole file a second time. A job that runs out of graphics memory is tried again one profile lighter, and the take records it. Other ways: From your phone: run gen serve --project with your project and press Start beside the file under Batches on the phone page. Start small: one prompt and one seed, to check the file. Then grow the matrix. Use a fast profile for a night of ideas, then retake the best at Quality.
Watch, pause and cancel jobs Watch the queue from your phone The VRAM scheduler Work faster

You get a take with the rumble, clicks, hiss and metallic shimmer taken out, and a dull top end brought back. Clean up is a step on Sound effect and Music assets, between the sound and its Effects. It's optional: with no Clean up take, Effects works from the sound directly. It works on made sounds and imported ones. the door creak before Clean up the door creak after Clean up at Strong
documents.s: Clean up a sound or track

documents.t: A Sound effect or Music asset with a take in use. For the two helper models: FlashSR (gen install weights --group flashsr), and SonicMaster, which is gated. Accept Stability AI's licence on Hugging Face, then gen install weights --group sonicmaster. If a model isn't installed, Clean up goes on without it and says so. In the app Command line Open the asset and click Clean up on the rail (or add it with the +). Set Strength: Gentle, Normal (the default) or Strong. It sets how hard hiss and shimmer are cut. Strong also removes clicks from a sound effect. Set Shimmer: Auto fixes the metallic flicker generators leave in the highs, when it's measured. Off leaves it. Strong always cuts it. For a track at the Quality profile, open Advanced and say what to fix in Music repair (less reverb, clearer vocals). Leave it empty for an all-round restore. Press New take. gen retake door_creak clean --set strength=strong --set shimmer=strong gen retake village_theme clean --profile quality --set instruction="less reverb" instruction is the form's Music repair.

Each sound is measured first, and only what the measurements show gets fixed. Then two models can help: Model When it runs What it does FlashSR Balanced and Quality, at PS3 or PS4, when the top end is dull (under 16 kHz) Restores the missing highs at 48 kHz SonicMaster A track at Quality Repairs and masters it, following Music repair After that, the take gets the era sound and loudness as usual. The progress line says what was fixed, and clean.json in the take has every measurement. On a sound effect with variants, pick the variants you want on the Clean up take before you go on. Effects uses the ones you pick. Start with Normal. Go to Strong only if hiss or clicks are left.
Layer a sound and add effects Sound for a game Steps and fields: audio_clean

You get bone chains down the parts that hang, and a Godot setup that swings them while the character moves. In Godot, a SpringBoneSimulator3D moves the chains. Nothing is baked into the clips, so the cloth reacts to whatever the character does in the game.
documents.s: Make hair, capes and skirts swing

documents.t: For long hair: a character with a Rig step. For a cape, skirt or coat: these aren't part of the character. Make them as wearables (see A base body and an outfit). In the app Command line Long hair on a character: Open the character and click Rig on the rail. Set Cloth. Auto (the default) adds chains when the description mentions hair: long hair, ponytail, braid. Hair always adds them. None never does. To change how it moves, open Advanced and set Cloth material. Press Retake in the title bar. A cape, skirt or coat as a wearable: Make a Wearable (under Characters & bodies in New asset), or open one. On its Design step, set Cloth to Auto, or pick Cape, Skirt, Hair, Tail or None. Set Cloth material under Advanced if Auto isn't right. Run the pipeline to Skin. The chains are added and checked there. gen retake courier skin --set cloth=hair --set cloth_material=chain gen retake red_cape wear_design --set cloth=cape --set cloth_material=leather skin is the Rig step's key. red_cape stands for a wearable of yours.

What Auto reads on a wearable: cape, cloak, mantle swing as a cape. Skirt, dress, robe, coat, kilt, tabard, gown as a skirt. Hair, ponytail, braid as hair. Tail, ribbon, scarf, tassel as a tail. The materials: Material Stiffness Drag Gravity For cloth 0.6 0.4 1.0 capes, skirts leather 1.4 0.5 0.8 coats, belts hair 0.9 0.3 0.6 hair, tails chain 0.4 0.2 1.6 chains, heavy jewellery Stiffness springs the chain back to its rest shape, drag damps the swing, gravity pulls it down. Auto uses cloth for capes and skirts, hair for hair and tails. What you get: A wearable's Skin take swings the chains in headless Godot before it's kept. If they stretch more than 5 %, the take fails and says why. With a display, the take also has a cloth.webp preview of the swing. The numbers are in wear.json under cloth_check. Export writes a .cloth.json beside the wearable, and for a character's own hair a .cloth.json and a ready _cloth.tscn scene named after the character. In Godot, Wearables.cloth() sets up the simulator from a .cloth.json (see Godot scripts). Capsule colliders on the hips, spine, chest and thighs, scaled to the character, keep the cloth out of the body.
How wearables, fitting and cloth work A base body and an outfit Export an asset to Godot

You get a new take of a composed piece with the bars you didn't like redrawn, your own notes where you wanted them, and the rest exactly as it was. A Composed music asset is written by rules from a style and a seed, with no model: its Compose step takes about 20 seconds on the CPU and gives a .mid for your DAW and a rendered preview. The editor changes that piece one bar, or one instrument in one bar, at a time.
documents.s: Edit a composed piece bar by bar

documents.t: You need a Composed music asset with a Compose take. The examples use the sample piece festival_waltz (style Gentle town). In the app Command line Open the asset, click Compose on the rail, and press Edit on a take. The strip on top is the piece: a chord card per bar, then a lane per instrument. Pick what to work on. Click an instrument's notes in a bar to work on that instrument there. Click the chord card to pick the whole bar. Shift-click picks a range. The line under the strip says what's picked, for example Bar 5 · all instruments. Press New idea for a fresh draw of what's picked. Press Rework rhythm or Rework pitches to vary the notes already there, yours included. Open the Takes tab. Each idea is listed there, with the notes it changed drawn brighter. Play one in place, pick the one to keep, or go back to Current. Open the Notes tab to write notes yourself. It is the piano roll of the picked instrument: click to draw, drag to move, drag an end to resize, right-drag to erase. Shift-click on a note stacks another. The drum kit is a step rack instead. The bars either side are shown dimmed. Press Lock on bars you're happy with. A locked bar is left alone by later re-rolls. The button reads Unlock when everything picked is locked. Press Space to play from the picked bar. Press Save as new take. It queues a Compose take from this take's seed and your edits. The take you opened stays as it was. Nothing changes until Save as new take. Undo and redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z) work on every edit before that. Edits go in the Compose step's edit field, separated by ;. They are applied to the newest take and keep its seed: gen retake festival_waltz compose --set edit="reroll 5; lock 3" gen retake festival_waltz compose --set edit="reroll_rhythm 7; reroll_pitch 8" gen retake festival_waltz compose --set edit="give 5 auto C5:8,E5:8" gen retake festival_waltz compose --set edit="reroll_part 5 kit; volume nylon -3" The number is a bar's id. Bar ids are in the take's piece.json. Action What it does reroll 5 a new draw of bar 5 reroll_rhythm 5, reroll_pitch 5 a new rhythm, or new pitches, for bar 5 lock 3, unlock 3 keep bar 3 out of re-rolls, or let it back in motif 7 make bar 7 the motif insert 5, insert end, delete 5 add a bar before bar 5 or after the last bar, or remove bar 5 give 5 auto C5:8,E5:8 your own bar, as typed notes give_midi 5 file.mid your own bar, from a MIDI file reroll_part 5 kit a new draw of one instrument in bar 5 rework 5 nylon rhythm a variation of one instrument's notes (rhythm or pitch) give_part 5 kit 0:1:36,8:1:38 your notes for one instrument, as on:length:pitch sound nylon 4, volume nylon -3, pan nylon -40 a part's General MIDI sound, its volume in dB, its pan kit and nylon are part names from a bossa nova piece. Yours depend on the style. A plain gen retake with no edit is a new piece, not an edit.

A new idea over your own notes: a new idea for a whole bar asks first when the bar has notes of yours. Keep my notes, re-roll the rest leaves them. Cue and loop: the ruler over the strip works like a DAW's. Click it to play from that beat. Drag along it to mark a span that Play loops. A click clears the span. With no span, the loop button repeats the picked bars. A line shows what's playing. Step through bars: the Left and Right arrow keys pick the bar before or after. Delete removes the notes picked in the roll. More room for notes: Full screen gives the roll the lanes' room. Back to all instruments returns. Sound, volume and pan: click an instrument's notes, then use the channel in the side panel. It gives the instrument another General MIDI sound (the kit: another drum kit), a volume and a pan. The instrument keeps its part in the music: only how it's played changes. Chords: the side panel lists the chords that fit the picked bar, best first. Click one to use it. Under them are Set as motif, Insert after, Copy to… and Delete. Longer or shorter sections: the − and + on a section's name remove or add a bar at its end. Everything at once: Re-roll every unlocked bar redraws all bars you haven't locked. Limits: an edit never changes another bar, so the bars either side of an insert or a delete keep their accompaniment. The piece is rendered through a General MIDI SoundFont. The .mid is what you take to a DAW for better sounds.
Split a track into stems and edit its MIDI: the MIDI editor for tracks that aren't composed. Layer a sound and add effects: the piece's Effects step. Steps and fields: compose Sound for a game

You get a Gen Studio dock in the Godot editor that shows the queue and imports finished assets with one button. The dock is a small editor plug-in. It shows and imports, and makes nothing itself. It talks to gen serve on your machine.
documents.s: Import from inside the Godot editor

documents.t: A Godot 4 project (a folder with project.godot). A Gen Studio project with some finished assets.

Install the dock into the Godot project: gen dock install ~/games/my-game It copies the add-on into addons/gen_studio/ and turns it on in project.godot. Start the server for your Gen Studio project, and leave it running: gen serve --project ~/gen/my-game-assets Open (or reopen) the game in Godot. The Gen Studio dock appears and says Connected. Read the dock's two lists, refreshed every few seconds (or press Refresh). Queue is what is running and waiting. Assets is each asset with its kind, marked stale when a step needs a rerun. Press Import beside an asset. Its files are copied into res://assets/gen/, the same as Export to Godot, and Godot imports them.

Another port: both commands use port 8765 by default. If you change it, use the same one for both: gen serve --port 9000 and gen dock install ~/games/my-game --port 9000. The token: the dock keeps the server's address and token in addons/gen_studio/server.json. The token stays the same across restarts, so you install the dock once. Don't commit server.json to a public repository: the token lets anyone on your network use the queue. A paused queue: the status line says Connected (paused). If it goes wrong: "gen serve: not reachable at …": start gen serve, or check the port matches. "… is not a Godot project": point gen dock install at the folder that holds project.godot. Import refuses a stale asset: rebuild its stale steps first. The dock doesn't show after install: reopen the project in Godot, or turn on Gen Studio under Project Settings → Plugins.
Export an asset to Godot Watch the queue from your phone: the same server, from your phone.

You get a new take where only the part you marked is repainted or remade. Everything outside it stays as it was: the same vertices, the same triangles, the same skin. Use it to fix a hand, swap a gauntlet or a helmet, add a piece (a pauldron, a handle), or repaint one glove.
documents.s: Change one part of a 3D model

documents.t: A model take: Mesh, Game mesh, Rig or Paint. Repaint needs a concept or a reference picture. Replace and Attach need the extensions gen.qwen-edit, gen.trellis2 and gen.concept to be on. In the app Command line Open the model's step, press Open large (the inspector), and press Select part. Click the part. Each click is a point SAM 3.1 looks for on four views of the model. Alt+click marks what is not the part. Or Shift+drag to brush over it: every face under the brush is taken as it is. [ and ] change the brush's size. Undo takes back the last mark, Clear starts again. Press Edit part…. An Edit part step is added after this one (on a new path when the step already has a next step) and opens with the part filled in, built from the take you marked. Set Mode: Repaint paints the part's texture again and keeps its shape. Replace remakes the part in 3D and joins it in its place. Attach makes a new piece there, as its own mesh. In What it should become, describe it: "a red leather glove", "an iron ring handle". Empty means the same part, sharper. Press New take in the title bar. The take shows the found part tinted orange (Painted region) beside the result. While you mark, right-drag turns the view, middle-drag pans and the wheel zooms. gen branch courier skin part_edit gen retake courier b1/part_edit --set "region=the left glove" --set mode=repaint \ --set "prompt=a red leather glove" gen retake courier b1/part_edit --set selection=.edits/courier/skin/selection-1a2b3c4d5e6f.json \ --set mode=replace --set "prompt=a steel gauntlet with five separate fingers" region names the part in words (the form's Or name it). selection is a JSON file the app writes when you mark a part: {"points": [{"p": [x, y, z], "n": [...], "sign": 1}], "brush": [{"p": [x, y, z], "r": 0.03}]}, in the model's own (glTF) space, rest pose.

Mode Takes about What happens Repaint 1.5 min Paint runs on the whole model, then bakes onto the part's faces only, feathered at the edge. With a prompt, Qwen-Image first redraws the part Replace 6 min Four views framed on the part are redrawn, cut out and built in 3D. The old faces go, and the new part is joined with a boolean union. Only a narrow seam may change Attach 6 min The same, but the new piece stays its own mesh and the model stays whole Edits that stack: on a take of an Edit part step, Select part and Edit part… start the next pass instead of a new step. The button then reads Build on Take N. On a rig, the new vertices get skin weights from the body around them, so the part moves with the skeleton. The record: part_edit.json beside the take says what happened, including a hash of the faces that had to stay, before and after. They match. One part at a time for Replace. A selection in two pieces remakes the larger. Click the middle of the part. A click on a glove often finds the forearm too. Alt+click the forearm to leave it out, or brush. A part the body hides (an armpit, the inside of a hand) is the weak spot. Brush it.
Repaint a model's texture Steps and fields: part_edit
You get an asset's finished result copied into your Godot project, ready to use.

A Godot 4 project: a folder with project.godot. The asset's steps finished, with no stale ones. Export refuses a stale asset, so Godot never gets a half-updated model. Rebuild the stale steps first. In the app Command line Open the asset. Press Export to Godot in the toolbar. The first time, pick your Godot project's folder. Gen Studio remembers it. Shift-click Export to Godot to pick another. Export to Godot on Home does every finished asset that isn't stale, at once. gen export lantern ~/games/my-game gen export courier ~/games/my-game --project ~/gen/my-game-assets gen export courier ~/games/my-game --step b1/retouch # the end of a path

Files land in res://assets/gen/ in a folder named after the asset, and shared scripts such as wearables.gd in res://assets/gen/. Export copies the takes in use: Asset Files Prop the Game mesh .glb; a toon scene when the project's toon look is on Character the rig .glb with every clip inside (Godot loops the *_loop clips); a .cloth.json and a _cloth.tscn scene when it has hair chains Wearable the .glb, .wardrobe.json, .cloth.json, and wardrobe.gd / wearables.gd Base body outfits.json and wardrobe.gd beside the body Texture its maps and a material.tres Effect the sprite sheet and its materials Sound, music .ogg with loop points (or WAV or FLAC) Dialogue Dialogue Manager files Anime set, 2D rig sprite_frames.tres, portrait.gd, Ren'Py files; the 2D rig's .tscn and its parts What the scripts do is in Godot scripts. Settings that change the export, in Settings → Project: Toon look in Godot: off for standard shading. On for cel shading and an outline, which adds a scene that puts the toon shader on every mesh. Export sounds and tracks as: OGG (small), WAV (24-bit, the loop in its smpl chunk) or FLAC (lossless, loop tags). Press Save in the Sound group. Good to know: Export again after a retake. The files are replaced in place, so scenes that use them pick up the change. To drag one file instead, use the handle at the bottom right of any output frame: drop it into Godot, Blender or a folder. "is not a Godot project": pick the folder that holds project.godot, not a subfolder. "has nothing to export yet": run the asset's steps first.
Import from inside the Godot editor Godot scripts Export and a small scene

You get the packs of steps you want: turning one on adds its steps, asset kinds and downloads, and turning one off takes them away. Most of Gen Studio's steps come from extensions: packs of steps, each with its own models and settings (gen.concept for concept art, gen.ace-step for music). Most are on. The anime pack, gen.anime, its add-on gen.anime-noobai and the pixel art and chiptune pack, gen.pixel, ship off. In the app Command line Open Settings (Ctrl+,) and pick Extensions. Search, or filter by category. Each row has a switch and its library, size on disk and description. Pick one to see its steps and models. Click the switch. Restart the app. Changes apply on the next start. If you turned one on, install its models under Settings → Models. Or don't: they download the first time a step needs them, after the app asks. gen ext list # every extension, on or off, and its stages gen ext enable gen.anime gen install weights --group anime gen ext disable gen.anime The switches are stored in the [extensions] table of ~/.config/gen-studio/config.toml.

What "off" means: an off extension adds nothing: no steps, no asset kinds, no fields, no downloads. Assets you made with it keep their folders and takes, but they stay out of the app until you turn the pack back on. Turning a pack off deletes nothing. Add-ons: an add-on offers another model for its parent's steps. gen.anime-noobai adds models to the anime pack's steps. It's active only while its parent is on, and the step then shows a Model choice beside Profile. The same set on another machine: gen update writes gen.lock from the installed extensions. gen restore installs exactly what it pins. Your own: put an extension folder in extensions/ of the Gen Studio folder, or in extensions/ of the data folder. See Write an extension. Turn off packs you don't use, to keep Settings → Models and New asset short.
Write an extension Run a step with a Kit Keep models on the drive you choose: models take space. The extensions, one page each Profiles and target looks

You get a free model, texture, sound, track, shader or voice as an asset in your project, with its licence and source recorded. Kind Libraries searched Models Poly Haven, ambientCG, Sketchfab, OpenGameArt Textures Poly Haven, ambientCG Sounds Openverse (Freesound), OpenGameArt Music Openverse, OpenGameArt Shaders Godot Shaders Voices AivisHub (Japanese voices) If one library is down, the others still answer.

You need an internet connection and an open project. Importing a model also needs Blender on your PATH. In the app Command line Open Find free assets: the magnifier beside New asset on the Assets page, File → Find free assets…, or New asset and then Free online assets. Pick a Kind. Type what you want (wooden chair, rain on a window) and press Search. Check each result's source and licence. Press Listen to hear a sound, track or voice, or Open page to see it in your browser. Press the import button: Prop or Character for a model, Import for the rest. The asset opens like one you made. Its first take is the imported file, and the licence and source are in its meta.json. gen find "wooden chair" gen find "brick wall" --textures gen find "rain on a window" --sounds gen find "calm village" --music gen find "dissolve" --shaders gen find "calm" --voices gen import polyhaven:brick_wall_001 --as texture gen import openverse:<id> --as sfx --asset rain_loop gen find prints each result's name (source:id), title and licence. gen import with that name and --as prop|character|texture|sfx|music|shader|voice brings one in.

Sketchfab downloads need your API token, in ~/.config/gen-studio/config.toml. Without it, Sketchfab results show only Open page. [assets] sketchfab_token = "your token" Some results can't be downloaded directly (gen find adds open and the page). Download those yourself, then import the file. An AivisHub voice is pinned by its file's sha256, so it can't change under you. Check the licence before you ship. CC0 needs nothing, CC-BY needs a credit. Gen Studio records it and doesn't decide for you. An imported sound goes through Clean up and Effects like a made one.
Bring in a model you already have Clean up a sound or track
You get a prop or character asset made from your own file, which you can paint, rig, give clips and export like a made one. Supported files: FBX, OBJ, GLB and glTF, VRM, and Blender's .blend.
documents.s: Bring in a model you already have

documents.t: Blender must be installed and on your PATH. It converts the file. In the app Command line Choose File → Import a model…, or New asset and then A 3D model under From a file. Pick Character model or Prop model. Fill in Asset name (lower-case letters, digits, _ and -). In Model file, pick the file. In Licence, say where it comes from and its licence (CC0, bought on a store). It's kept with the take. Leave your own for your own work. Press Generate. The quickest way skips the form: drop the file on Home's prompt bar. gen import my_knight.fbx --as character gen import crate.blend --as prop --asset old_crate gen import ~/models/lamp.glb --as prop --licence "CC-BY 4.0, the author's name" Without --asset, the name comes from the file name. Without --licence, it is recorded as your own.

Blender converts the file to one GLB, which becomes the asset's Game mesh take, and renders a front view, which becomes a Concept take. You can vary or restyle that render like any concept. A prop is ready to paint and export. A rigged humanoid gets its Rig take straight away. Its bones are mapped to Godot's humanoid names, so clips work at once. An unrigged character runs the Rig step next. The model is kept as it is: its triangles aren't cut down to the target look's budget. "Blender is not on PATH": install Blender, or put it on your PATH, then retake the step.
Find and import free assets: a free model imports the same way. Repaint a model's texture: give it a new look. Steps and fields: import_model

You get a take made with a different recipe for the step: another model, its limits, sometimes a LoRA, and passes that run after it. A Kit is optional. Everything runs on Default, which is no Kit at all.
documents.s: Run a step with a Kit

documents.t: A step that has Kits. It shows a row of picture cards above its form. Some Kits need a LoRA file. Some Civitai files need a login: add your key in Settings → Downloads. Early Access files have to be unlocked on Civitai first. In the app Command line Open the step. Above its form is a row of picture cards: Default and one card per Kit. Click a Kit's card. The form shrinks to what that Kit lets you change (the prompt and its Steps), and the prompt guide, the sparkle and the dice follow the Kit's style. If the card shows a download icon, the Kit needs a LoRA you don't have. Choose Download, or Add file… for a file you got yourself. Make a take as usual. The Kit's models download the first time you run it, like any optional model. gen kit list # the Kits, and what each still needs gen retake <asset> <step> --set kit=anime-in-real --set prompt="..." gen kit download anime-in-real # the Kit's LoRA gen kit add-file anime-in-real ~/Downloads/lora.safetensors add-file is for a file you downloaded yourself. It checks the sha256.

Kit and Profile: the Kit is the style and the model. Profile stays for speed against quality, but a Kit can pin everything, and the shipped ones do. Community Kits: gen kit install https://example.com/some/kits.git gen kit install ~/my-kits gen kit remove <id> A Kit is a folder: kit.toml, guide.toml and a preview picture. It holds no code, and names a model family Gen Studio already ships, so installing one runs nothing. Yours are kept in kits/ in the data folder. Steps that can't follow: Rim light, Retouch and character LoRAs are built on Anima. On a picture made with a Kit of another model they refuse, and say why. An optional LoRA: a Kit can mark its LoRA optional = true. Until the file is installed the Kit runs without it and without its trigger word, and the card says so.
Turn extensions on and off Write a prompt the model understands

You get each extension's models on the drive you pick, and a way to move them later. It works like a game launcher's library folders. A library is a folder on any drive where models and their environments live. Your data folder is the first library, Data folder. Add a library on another drive, and you can install an extension there or move one there later. Nothing is tied to one drive.
documents.s: Keep models on the drive you choose

documents.t: You need a drive with free space. Some drives (exFAT or FAT USB sticks) can't hold environments: such a library shows Models only, and those extensions keep their environments in the Data folder. In the app Command line Open Settings (Ctrl+,) and pick Storage. Under Libraries, press Add library… and pick a folder on the drive. Check the drive, its filesystem and free space, give it a name (Games SSD, say), and press OK. Gen Studio makes a gen-studio-library folder there, with a small library.json that names it. To move an extension there, go to Settings → Extensions and pick the extension. Its Storage group shows which library it is in and how much it takes. Press Move… and pick the library. Each one says whether it fits ("37 GB fits · 140 GB left after") or how much it is short. Choose what happens to the old copy: Keep the old copy in the trash (the default), or Delete the old copy, which asks you in red first. Press Move. The progress shows in the Storage group. Cancel keeps what was copied, and Move… again carries on from there. gen library add /mnt/games --label "Games SSD" gen library list gen ext move gen.vfx "Games SSD" # old copy to the library's .trash/ gen ext move gen.vfx "Games SSD" --delete-old # asks first; --yes doesn't gen install weights --group vfx-video-14b --library "Games SSD" An interrupted gen ext move carries on when you run it again.

Every model file is checked by its sha256 before anything switches. Environments are rebuilt from their lockfiles on the new drive, not copied. If a model is shared with another extension (the text encoder of both Wan models, say), it moves too, and the other extension reads it from the new drive. The dialog says so.

Make default on a library sends new extensions there (gen library default with its id). When a step needs a model that isn't installed, the prompt says which library it downloads to and how much is free there. Change… lists your libraries with their free space. For an extension that isn't placed anywhere yet, the one you pick becomes its library. For one that already lives on another library, choose Just this download (only this model goes there) or the choice that moves the extension there too (the move runs first, then the download). Setup's Where models go step does the same for everything at once: pick a drive, and a library is made there at Install.

Its library shows Drive missing, and so do its extensions. A step that needs it says which drive to connect and offers Retry. Nothing is downloaded again in the meantime. Plug it back in at the same place and everything works again. You don't need to restart (the app checks every 10 s). If it mounts somewhere else now, press Relocate… on its row, or run gen library add with the new place. It is found by its library.json, keeps its name, and the links are updated.
Remove… only forgets the library. Nothing on the drive is deleted. It is greyed out while extensions or files are still there: move them first.

gen doctor lists each library (free space, whether it is connected) and checks every link: links to a missing drive; files that are on a library other than where their extension is placed; leftovers nothing uses; foreign links, which point into a folder that is no library (models you moved by hand, say). Fix them with gen library add on a folder on that drive with --adopt, which moves those files into the library instantly. If the links get lost (a broken move, a reinstall), gen doctor --relink rebuilds them from the libraries. Add --verify to match files by sha256 instead of size.
Move the data folder to another disk: the Data folder itself, with the runtimes and gen.db. Turn extensions on and off

You get a track's parts as separate stems, a MIDI file of each, and a way to change the notes. Both are optional steps on a Music asset. They never run by themselves: you add them. A sound effect or effect can have a MIDI step too.
documents.s: Split a track into stems and edit its MIDI

documents.t: You need a Music asset with a take in use (see Sound for a game). A piece from the composer has its own editor: see Edit a composed piece bar by bar. In the app Command line Open the track and press the + on the rail. Pick Stems. Press New take. You get drums, bass, vocals and the rest. Each stem can be soloed or muted. Press the + again and pick MIDI. Press New take. It writes a MIDI file of each stem, and a preview of the song played with General MIDI instruments. Press Edit MIDI on the MIDI take. Pick a row in the Channel rack on the left: one row per stem. Under the rows, set the picked one's sound (a General MIDI instrument, or a drum kit), volume and pan. Change the notes. Drums are a step rack of 16 steps a bar, a row per drum: click a step to add or take away a hit. Everything else is a piano roll with a Velocity lane under it. Press the play button in the top bar to hear your edit, then Save. Save changes the take you opened, and steps after it are marked stale. The take as it was goes to the project's .trash folder. gen add-step village_theme music stems gen run-to village_theme stems gen run-to village_theme midi # adds and runs what it needs on the way Editing notes has no command. The MIDI files are in the take's folder for your DAW.

A new part under the same song: New take on a stem writes a new part: a new bass line, say. The piano roll: snap runs from 1/4 to 1/16. Shift + click on a note stacks another on it. Timing tools, above the grid: Line up with the beat, Snap to audio, Quantize (with Strength, Swing and Ends), and Clean up (with Legato). The ruler over the grid: click it to play from there, drag along it to mark bars that Play loops. Play while you edit: an edit while it plays comes in where it is. Undo and redo are Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z. The editor is built from the same parts as the composer's editor: the same top bar with the transport, the same ruler, step rack, piano roll and channel panel.
Edit a composed piece bar by bar Sound for a game Layer a sound and add effects

You get a new take of a sound or track with other sounds stacked under it and a rack of effects on it. What you hear is live: nothing is rendered until you save. The mixer is the centre of a sound's or track's Effects step.
documents.s: Layer a sound and add effects

documents.t: You need a Sound effect or Music asset whose first step has a take in use (see Sound for a game). In the app Command line Open the asset and click Effects on the rail (or add it with the +). Pick the New take card in the strip. To start from a take instead, pick it and press Edit in the mixer. Press Add layer… and pick where the layer comes from: one of the project's sounds by name, Find a match… (the project's sounds, each with the part it would fill), From a file…, or Generate a layer…. On the layer's row, set the part it fills: Full, Transient (the first 80 ms, the snap), Body, Low end or Tail. Then set Gain, Pan and Pitch. Drag the layer along its lane to set where it starts, or press Align to line its attack up with the sound's. Press Add effect… to add a slot to the rack. Pick a slot to see its settings on the right, as knobs and faders. Press New take. The layers and rack are rendered into a new take, at the loudness its Role sets. A new layer starts 6 dB under, lined up with the sound's attack. gen retake door_creak effects --set role=ambience --set loop=true The form's fields are set with --set: role, loop (Seamless loop), channels. The rack is a JSON value of the chain field. Layers are easier to set in the app. The keys are in steps and fields.

Generate a layer…: describe it (a deep sub-bass thump) and press Generate. It makes a new Sound effect asset as long as this sound. Pick a variant there, then add it here. Suggest layers asks the writing helper for ideas. Hear one layer: press S on a layer to hear it alone. The light at the left of a row turns the layer off. A quick rack: open Quick setup in the inputs. Pick plain choices (Tone, Body, Punch, Character, Room, Amount) and press Fill the rack, or type a description in Describe it (distant, metallic, in a cave) and press From the words. Start from… loads a ready-made rack. What's in Add effect…: effects are grouped by what they do: EQ and filters, Dynamics, Distortion, Modulation, Delay, Reverb, Pitch and time, Multi-effect, Utility, Your plugins. VST3 plugins in ~/.vst3, /usr/lib/vst3 or /usr/local/lib/vst3 are listed too. A plugin has Plugin window, for its own interface. A slot's controls: a light (on and off), a wet/dry knob, and a ⋯ menu with settings, move, duplicate and remove. Drag the grip to reorder. Compare: the bypass button over the slots plays the sound without the rack, at the same loudness. Compare on the transport shows the input as a ghost behind the waveform. Role sets the loudness and whether the sound is mono (placed in 3D) or stereo. Channels overrides that. Turn on Seamless loop for ambiences: the end cross-fades into the start. Every take records the settings of each slot, so a take made with Quick setup can be remade exactly.
Clean up a sound or track: fix noise before the effects. Steps and fields: audio_fx

You get Gen Studio's data folder on a bigger disk, with a link at the old path so every setting keeps working. The data folder holds the model weights, the worker environments, the managed ComfyUI and llama.cpp, caches and gen.db. It's ~/.local/share/gen-studio/ by default and can grow past 100 GB. Your projects live elsewhere and aren't moved. To keep only the models on another drive, use libraries instead. It's the simpler choice for most people.
documents.s: Move the data folder to another disk

documents.t: An empty folder on the new disk, with room for everything. What uses the space on the Storage page, or gen data usage, tells you how much. Nothing running: let the queue finish or pause it. In the app Command line Open Settings (Ctrl+,) and pick Storage. Under Data folder, press Move… and pick the empty folder. Wait for it to finish. It copies everything, checks every file arrived at its size, then leaves a link at the old path. When it says Moved, it shows where the old copy is: the old folder, renamed with .moved- and the time. Delete that copy yourself once everything works. gen data usage # what uses the space, biggest first gen data move /mnt/bigdisk/gen-studio gen doctor # check the disk, GPU and runtimes after To move it back, run gen data move with the original path: the link is replaced by the real folder.

What uses the space on the Storage page (or gen data usage) lists, biggest first: each extension's weights, each project, caches, runtimes, worker environments, and weight files no installed extension names (orphans). Remove beside weights deletes those model files. Steps that need them won't run until you install them again. Remove beside a cache is safe: it is rebuilt as you use the app.

If you downloaded some weights before (for ComfyUI, say), Gen Studio can use them instead of downloading again. Press Import model files… on the Storage page and pick the folder that holds them. Every file whose size and sha256 match a pinned weight is linked (or copied) into place. gen data import ~/ComfyUI/models
documents.s: Reuse model files you already have

documents.t: Under Old takes, the last group on the Storage page, Gen Studio counts the takes in this project that are not in use, not favourites, and over 14 days old. Move to .trash moves them to the project's .trash/. Nothing is deleted until you empty .trash/ yourself.
To start with the data folder somewhere else, set data_dir in ~/.config/gen-studio/config.toml before the first install. The uv cache (~/.cache/uv) is separate and can be large too. It isn't moved.
Keep models on the drive you choose: each extension on its own drive. Turn extensions on and off: turning off a pack you don't use stops its downloads. Why local
You get the same game mesh with a new texture, painted from a picture by Hunyuan3D-Paint and baked onto the mesh's own UVs. The mesh, its UVs and its rig stay as they are.

A prop or character with a Game mesh take, made or imported. About 21 GB of free graphics memory, and 4 to 7 minutes. Paint is one of the heaviest steps. The Paint model's weights. If they're missing, the app asks before it downloads them. Hunyuan3D-Paint has a non-commercial licence that excludes the EU, the UK and South Korea. Gen Studio records it in the take. In the app Command line Open the asset and add Paint with the + on the rail, after the Game mesh. It's optional, and Run to end skips it. Leave Reference image empty to paint from the concept in use (and, for a character, its turnaround). Or pick your own picture. Press New take in the title bar. The take is the game mesh with the new texture. On a character, the Rig step is built from the painted mesh, so it turns stale if it already ran. gen add-step market_cart retopo paint gen run-to market_cart paint gen retake market_cart paint --set region="the awning" --set mix=0.7 image, region and mix are the form's Reference image, Only paint and Paint strength. To paint another take of the Game mesh or the Rig as a new take of that same step, name it with paint_from: gen retake market_cart retopo --set paint_from=2 gen retake courier skin --set paint_from=1 --set region="the boots" --set mix=0.7

In Only paint, name the part as you'd point at it: the awning, the boots. Lower Paint strength below 1 to keep some of the model's own texture under the paint. Press New take. The rest keeps its texture. With a part named, Build on Take N paints on that take, so parts stack. A whole repaint starts from the step before. To mark the part by hand in 3D, use Change one part of a 3D model.

This is how to give an imported model a new look. Click Concept on the rail and pick a take (for an imported model, its render). Press Restyle…, describe the look in What it should look like (a weathered bronze lantern) and press Restyle. You get a new concept take with the same outline. Use that take, then run Paint. gen retake lantern concept --set control=renders/lantern.png --prompt "a weathered bronze lantern"

New maps baked onto your mesh's own UVs. Which ones depends on the target look: base colour at PS1 and PS2, plus roughness at PS3, plus metallic at PS4. At PS1 and PS2 the base colour also gets a palette, the same readability pass as the original texture.

"Paint needs a Game mesh take first": run the steps up to Game mesh. Out of memory: close other GPU programs. It looks wrong from behind: the concept shows only the front. Characters use their turnaround too. For a prop, give it a reference picture that shows more.
Change one part of a 3D model Change one part of a concept by naming it Bring in a model you already have Steps and fields: paint

You get an asset with the steps you want: the next one added, another route tried from any step, and what you don't need taken away. The rail shows only the steps an asset has. In the app Command line Add a step: press the dashed + at the end of a row on the rail. Add step lists what can follow, under headings (Edit, Make 3D, Rig and motion, Animate, Sound, Text, Shader). Each card says what the step does, the model it runs at this profile and about how long it takes. The first card, marked Recommended, is the step the asset's template runs next. Pick one, and its form opens. A download icon beside its time means its model isn't installed yet: the app asks before it downloads. Branch from a step: hover a pill and press the small + under it, or right-click it and choose Branch from here…. Pick the step. The new path is a row of its own on the rail, named b1, b2 and so on, with its own takes, steps and colour. Skip a step: right-click an optional step and choose Skip this step. It's drawn dashed and dimmed, and the steps after it build as if it weren't there. Delete a step: right-click it and choose Delete step…. The dialog lists what goes with it: the step, the steps after it on its path, and any paths and clips leaving from those, each with its take count. Everything moves to the project's .trash/. You can't delete an asset's first step. gen add-step lantern retopo paint # Paint after the Game mesh gen run-to lantern paint # run up to it gen branch lantern retopo paint # a new path from the Game mesh gen retake lantern b1/paint # a take on that path gen delete-step lantern paint # asks first; --yes doesn't gen ext list shows the stage names add-step and branch take. There is no command for skipping a step.
documents.s: Add, branch, skip and delete steps

documents.t: Run the next step from the take you're on: when a later step exists, the title bar's ⋯ menu has Run next: with its name. On a take that isn't in use, Use and run does both. Build from an older take without a new path: right-click the take in the strip and choose Build next step from this take. A branch is the way to try a different finish without losing the one you have. gen export takes --step b1/paint to export the end of a path.
Rebuild the stale steps Takes, stale steps and provenance Steps and fields

You get a page on your phone that shows what you generated, lets you pick takes, shows the queue and the GPU, pauses the queue and starts a batch while the machine works. The page runs on your own machine and is reachable only on your local network. Nothing goes through the internet.
documents.s: Watch the queue from your phone

documents.t: Your phone and the Gen Studio machine on the same network (Wi-Fi or LAN). A Gen Studio project. For batches, YAML files in its batches/ folder (see Run many jobs overnight).

On the Gen Studio machine, start the server for the project: gen serve --project ~/gen/my-game-assets It prints a line like Gen Studio on your phone: http://192.168.1.20:8765/?t=…. Open that whole URL on your phone. The ?t=… part is the token. Without it the page refuses every request. Bookmark it: the token stays the same across restarts. Under Recent generations, tap a picture for full size and how it was made. Use makes that take the one in use, as Use this take does in the app. Under Queue, press Pause to stop new jobs from starting and Resume to start them again. Below it are the files in the project's batches/ folder: Start queues one at low priority and starts working through the queue. Press Ctrl+C on the machine to stop the server.

The page's sections, top to bottom (on a wider screen the last three sit beside the pictures): Recent generations: the newest takes in the project. In use marks the current one. Check it marks a review step waiting for you to look at it, which you continue in the app. A phone shows the newest six. Show all shows the rest, up to 24. Running: what is running, with its progress and time left, then how many are waiting and any recent failures. The time left comes from how long this kind of step took lately, so the first run of a step shows only the time so far. Machine: how busy the GPU is, its VRAM and the machine's memory. Queue: pause, resume and batches. Options: gen serve --project ~/gen/my-game-assets --port 9000 # another port (default 8765) gen serve --project ~/gen/my-game-assets --host 127.0.0.1 # this machine only The default host, 0.0.0.0, makes the page reachable from your network. Good to know: A take with no picture (a model, a sound) gets a tile with its kind. Open those in the app. Keep gen serve running while you use the page. Stopping it closes the page. Jobs already running go on. Using a take from the phone marks the steps after it stale, as in the app. Rerun them later from the app or with gen rerun-stale and the asset's name. The token lives in the data folder. Anyone with the full URL on your network can use the page, so don't share it. The page doesn't load: check both devices are on the same network, and that a firewall on the machine allows the port. "open the URL gen serve printed (it has the token)": open the full URL with its ?t=… part.
Run many jobs overnight Import from inside the Godot editor: the same server, inside the Godot editor. A clip from your phone: a different thing, motion capture from a video.

You get a prompt written the way the step's model wants it, and a way to keep the ones that work. Each model wants a prompt written its own way. Gen Studio has four helpers: the writing helper, the prompt guide, your saved prompts, and presets for the rest of the form.
documents.s: Write a prompt the model understands

documents.t: Open a step with a Prompt field (a prop's Concept, say) and write what you want in your own words. Press the sparkle beside the prompt. The writing helper rewrites what you wrote the way this step's model wants it. It is a small model that runs on your CPU, so it never takes the GPU, and it answers in about two seconds. An undo arrow puts back what you had. On an empty prompt, press the dice instead: you get a new prompt in the style of the guide's examples. Press (i) beside the prompt to open the prompt guide. It has a tab per model, the profile's model first: a summary, the structure the model likes, tips, what to avoid, your prompts and examples. Use fills the field. Press the star beside a prompt that worked to save it for that stage. It shows in the guide under your prompts. Delete it there. There is no command-line form of the helpers. On the command line, the prompt is --prompt on gen retake and gen make, or prompt: in a job file.

A name from the prompt: the sparkle on a name field makes a name from the prompt, unique in the project. Enhance the prompt on some steps is different: a larger text model rewrites the prompt when the step runs, and the rewrite is saved with the take. Presets, for the rest of a form: open Advanced, press Save as preset, and name it. Use fills the form from it, for that stage in every project. A step with no take yet starts from the values you used last for that stage. Every step's guide is also on its wiki page, under Tips (for example Concept). What to say: Say what it is, what it's made of and how worn it is. Gen Studio adds the camera and background a step needs, so leave those out. One thing per prompt. A table with a lamp on it makes one fused piece. Change one thing per take, so you know what made the difference.
Make more takes and keep the best Change one part of a concept by naming it

You see what's running and what's waiting, hold the queue, and stop or retry a job. One big model fits on the GPU at a time, so jobs wait their turn. Everything you start goes in the queue, across all your projects. Downloads have a lane of their own beside the GPU job. In the app Command line Look at the status bar, at the bottom: the running job and its progress, then CPU, RAM, GPU and graphics memory. Press Queue at its right end to open the list. Each row links to its step. Rows run newest first, so the running job is at the bottom. Press Pause in the queue's header to hold it. The running job finishes, and nothing new starts. Resume starts them again. Hover a row. Cancel stops a queued or running job, and Retry starts a failed or cancelled one again. gen queue run # work through queued jobs without the app gen queue run is the only queue command. To see or steer the queue away from the app, use the phone page.

Cancel everything a step has going: right-click it on the rail and choose Cancel its runs. On Home: On the GPU shows the running job, what's next and what's holding the memory. When a job fails: the row and the step's failure panel say what went wrong in plain words, and what to do. Retake tries again, Copy log copies the job's log. Out of graphics memory: the job goes again one profile lighter by itself, and the take says so: "Fell back: ran at Fast". See the VRAM scheduler. Get told when it's done: a job that finishes or fails while the window is in the background sends a desktop notification.
Run many jobs overnight Watch the queue from your phone Troubleshooting

You get the same take again with a new seed, in the same place in the strip, without adding another take. Use it when a take is close but has one bad roll (a broken hand, a muddy sound) and you don't want to keep the bad one. To keep both, make a new take instead. In the app Command line Open the asset and click the step on the rail. Right-click the take in the strip. Choose Reroll (replace this take). The step runs again with a new seed. The new take goes where the old one was. If the old take was in use, the new one is used instead, and the steps after it turn stale. gen reroll lantern concept # the take in use gen reroll lantern concept 2 # Take 2 (v002)
documents.s: Replace a take with a new roll

documents.t: Where the old one goes: its pictures are copied into the new take's rerolls/ folder, so you can look back at them. The old take, with its other files, goes to the project's .trash/. Nothing is deleted. Empty .trash/ yourself when you're sure. Reroll changes only the seed. To change the prompt or a slider, use Retake. The new take has its own seed in its meta.json, so it stays reproducible.
Make more takes and keep the best Rebuild the stale steps
You get several takes of one step, see them side by side, and choose the one the next step uses.
documents.s: Make more takes and keep the best

documents.t: You need an asset whose step has run at least once (see your first prop). The examples use the sample prop lantern. In the app Command line Open the asset and click the step on the rail. Change what you want in the inputs on the left: the prompt, the Profile, a slider. Leave them alone for the same settings with a new seed. Press Retake in the step's title bar (R). On the New take card in the strip, the same button reads New take. The new take appears in the strip while it runs. The take in use stays in use, so nothing after it changes yet. To compare, hover a take card and tick the box in its corner, or Ctrl-click it. Pick two or more, then press Compare N in the title bar. Click the take you want, then press Use this take in the title bar (U). When there is a step after it, the button reads Use and run with that step's name, and starts it too. The steps built from the old take are now stale. gen retake lantern concept --prompt "a brass lantern with green glass panes" gen retake lantern retopo --set triangles=2000 --profile balanced gen status lantern # every step's takes, the one in use, stale steps gen promote lantern concept 3 # use Take 3 (v003) gen discard lantern concept 2 # Take 2 to the project's .trash/ --set takes any field of the step's form by its key. The keys are in steps and fields. A take from gen retake is kept, but not used until you promote it.

Your own seed: each take gets a new random seed while the shuffle button beside Seed is on. Turn it off to set one. Without opening the step: right-click the step on the rail and choose Retake. Use without running on: hover a take in the strip and press its check mark, or double-click it, or right-click it and choose Use this take. The small arrow on Use and run goes on from the take already in use instead. What Compare shows: the same output of each take side by side, with its stats. 3D views turn and zoom together. Sounds stop the others when one plays, and they are matched in loudness, so you compare the sound and not the level. Mark the good ones: right-click a take for Favourite and a rating from 1 to 5. Throw one away: Discard… moves a take to the project's .trash/. You can't discard the take in use. Reuse settings: Advanced under the inputs has Save as preset for values you use again. Change one thing per take. Then you know what made the difference.
Replace a take with a new roll: a new seed that replaces a take instead of adding one. Rebuild the stale steps Takes, stale steps and provenance
You get a new take with one area redrawn, and every other pixel as it was. Use it to fix a hand or a face, to change one part ("make the glass green"), or to keep only the good parts of a rim light.

You need a picture take: a concept, an anime image or shot, a texture, any step that makes a picture. It must be the take in use. In the app Command line Open the picture's step and show the take you want to fix. Press Retouch… in the title bar. A Retouch step is added after this one and opens. If the step already has a next step, it goes on a new path. In the form, press Draw the area… and paint over what to repaint. The editor opens on the picture you're about to change. Press Apply. Set Model. Same as the picture redraws with the model that drew it. Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 changes the area by an instruction instead. Set Strength. 0.3 to 0.5 keeps the shape and colour and fixes detail. 0.5 to 0.7 reinterprets. 1.0 draws it anew from what's around it. Check the Prompt: it is the picture's own, filled in. With Qwen, write The change instead ("make the glass green"). Press New take in the title bar. The mask editor's tools: Tool Key What it does Brush B Paint the area. Set size ([ and ], or Ctrl + wheel) and hardness Eraser E Paint it away Lasso, Box L, R Fill a shape Click K SAM 3.1 finds the part you click. Alt-click cuts, drag for a box Find by name SAM 3.1 finds the part you name The wheel zooms at the cursor, middle-drag or Space-drag pans, Ctrl+Z undoes. Hold \ to see the picture without the area. Click and Find by name need ComfyUI running, which any job starts. gen branch courier concept retouch gen retake courier b1/retouch --set mask=hand.png --set strength=0.5 gen retake courier b1/retouch --set mask=hand.png --set "model=Qwen-Image-Edit 2511" \ --set "change=make the satchel red" gen retake courier b1/retouch --set mask=face.png --set base=2 # from Take 2 mask is an 8-bit PNG at the picture's size (white: repaint, grey: partly, black: keep), relative to the project. gen branch starts the Retouch step on a new path, b1.

Pick a take of the Retouch step: everything in the form now works on it. Build on Take 2 starts a new take from Take 2's picture, so fixes stack: Take 1 fixes the hand, Take 2 the face. The area stays, with Clear beside it, since you often go over the same spot. Retake, in the title bar's ⋯ menu, repeats Take 2's settings from where Take 2 started, to try that pass again. It keeps the seed unless you change it or turn on the random seed. On New take, Starts from picks the picture it starts from: Original (the step before's take) by default, or any take. If the concept changes under a stack, the takes are marked stale and stay that way until you rebuild them.
Fix hands and Fix face (under Preset) find each hand or the face and redraw it up close, with nothing to draw.

On a Rim light or Relight take, press Erase parts…. Paint over the light you don't want. The picture before the step shows through. The eraser paints the light back. Press Make the take. It's made on your CPU in a second or two, without running the model. gen retake noa_hero anime_rim --set erase=too_much.png --set erase_from=3
documents.s: Erase parts of a Rim light or Relight

documents.t: Mark a little past the part. Grow and Soft edge (under Advanced) blend it in, and nothing outside the mark changes. A colour a shade off? Match colour (on by default) shifts the repaint to the colours around it. Not what you wanted? Reroll for another seed.
Change one part of a concept by naming it: the same idea on a concept, by name only. Make more takes and keep the best Steps and fields: retouch

You get Gen Studio installed, with the models for what you want to make downloading in the background while you use the app. The first time you open Gen Studio, a Set up Gen Studio window opens over the app. You make a few choices, and each kind of asset works as soon as its models arrive.
documents.s: Install and set up Gen Studio

documents.t: Linux and an NVIDIA GPU. Gen Studio is built and tested on an RTX 4090 with 24 GB. Many steps want 16 to 24 GB of graphics memory. Smaller cards can run the Fast profile and fall back when a step doesn't fit. With no NVIDIA GPU, you can point it at a ComfyUI on another machine. Disk space. 80 GB for the Minimal tier, 266 GB for Recommended, 358 GB for Full. The setup window shows the exact plan per drive before anything downloads. Godot 4, for your game. Blender on your PATH. The game mesh step, Paint and importing models use it. gen doctor says whether it's found. uv, to install. While Kasumi, the app's UI framework, is a private repository, installing also needs SSH access to it on GitHub.

packaging/install.sh # from a checkout: installs gen, gen-app and gen-mcp gen-app # opens the app and the setup window There's also an AUR package, packaging/aur/PKGBUILD. In the app Command line The steps are on the left, and you can go back to any of them. The plan, under them, shows where models go, the tier, the packs, what downloads and how much room is left. It changes as you choose. Welcome: Express takes the suggestion for this machine and goes straight to the plan. Custom shows every step. Not now closes the window. Home then shows a row to finish setup, with Open setup. System check: the GPU and its memory, the driver and CUDA, RAM, each drive's free space, uv and Hugging Face. It never stops you. It says which profile new assets start at: Balanced from 20 GB of graphics memory, else Fast. Where models go: one row per drive, with what the plan needs against its free space. Your data folder stays where it is. Pick another drive and the models go to a library there. Choose folder… picks any folder. What to install: the tier, Minimal (props and characters at Fast), Recommended (every kind at Fast and Ultra fast) or Full (every profile). Then the packs: 3D, Audio, Effects, Text and LLM, Anime (off by default) and Gated models. An unticked pack isn't switched off: its models download the first time you use them, after the app asks. Import models: model folders you already have (ComfyUI's models/, the Hugging Face cache, Stability Matrix, LM Studio). Ticked files are checked by sha256 and linked, so they aren't downloaded again. Skip if you have none. On the same page you can paste a Civitai API key. Leave it empty to skip (Settings → Downloads has it too). Install: queues the work: imports, ComfyUI, the model environments, llama.cpp, then each pack's models. Each is a row with its progress, and they carry on after a restart. Continue in background closes the window. Ready: each pack is ready, downloading, queued, on first use or off. Make a first prop opens New asset. gen setup # the same questions, the suggestion as the default gen setup --express --yes # take the suggestion and install gen setup --tier minimal --packs 3d,audio --library /mnt/games --dry-run # the plan and sizes only gen setup --status # per pack: ready, downloading, on first use gen setup --resume # queue again what failed gen config civitai-key --set # the Civitai API key gen doctor # check the GPU, driver, disk and runtimes gen setup follows the downloads until they finish. Ctrl-C stops following. The jobs stay queued, and the app or gen queue run carries on.
Settings → Setup → Open setup reopens the window. Install then queues only what's new: a pack you ticked, a bigger tier, models on another drive. To remove models, use Settings → Models.
Your first launch: the window and one picture, in ten minutes. A tour of the app Keep models on the drive you choose Troubleshooting

You get an asset whose every step is made from the takes now in use. A step is stale when a take it was made from is no longer in use. Say you use concept Take 3 instead of Take 1: the Prepped cut-out, Mesh and Game mesh were made from Take 1, so they are stale until they run again. Stale isn't an error. The old results are still there.

Find what's stale: On the rail, stale steps have the stale colour. The step's title bar says stale: and what changed. Home's Waiting for you has a card for it, and Assets has a Stale filter. In the app Command line Open the asset. Press Re-run stale in the toolbar. It only shows when something is stale. Each stale step runs again from the takes now in use, in order. Each makes a new take, and that take is used. Every step costs what it cost the first time. gen status lantern # lists the stale steps gen rerun-stale lantern # every stale step, a character's clips too gen run-to lantern retopo # only up to the Game mesh

Run to end runs every step that's missing or stale, to the end or the next review. Right-click a step and choose Run to here to rebuild up to that one only. Auto-continue makes a finished step start the next one by itself, up to the next review. It's set per project. Liked the old result better? Use the old take again, and the steps after it aren't stale any more. Export to Godot refuses a stale asset, so Godot never gets a half-updated model.

A take made with Build on Take N (a stack of Retouch or Edit part passes, say) gets its picture from that other take, not from the step before. Running it again would keep the old pixels, so Re-run stale and Run to here leave it, and the steps after it, marked: the title bar says rebuild by hand. To rebuild one, start from New take on that step, with Starts from set to Original, and make the passes again. Or use the old take of the step before again, and the mark goes.
Make more takes and keep the best Takes, stale steps and provenance

You get a new concept take with one named part redrawn, and every other pixel as it was. Use it when a concept is right except for one thing: the handle, a sleeve, the colour of a cloak. It's faster than retaking until the whole picture comes out right.
documents.s: Change one part of a concept by naming it

documents.t: You need an asset with a Concept take. To mark the area by hand, or to fix a picture that isn't a concept, use Retouch. In the app Command line Open the asset, click Concept on the rail, and click the take you want to change. Press Vary region… in the title bar. In What to change, name the part as you'd point at it: the handle, the left sleeve. In Change it to, say what it should become: a twisted iron handle, a torn red sleeve. Press Vary. SAM 3.1 finds the part you named, and only that part is redrawn. The result is a new take. The take you varied stays as it was. gen retake lantern concept --set vary_from=2 --set region="the handle" \ --prompt "a twisted iron handle" vary_from is the take to change. Add --set grow=32 to let the redraw reach further past the part's edge (16 pixels by default) so it blends in.

Keep the region short and concrete. The helmet works better than the thing on his head. Describe only the new part in Change it to, not the whole picture. See a seam at the edge? Vary again with a larger grow. To change the whole look but keep the outline, use Restyle… (see Repaint a model's texture). Then use the varied take, and rebuild the stale steps so the model is made from it.
Repaint part of a picture Make more takes and keep the best

You get a step of your own in Gen Studio: a manifest that describes it, a worker that does the work in its own environment, and the checks that say it's fit to use. An extension is a folder with a gen-extension.toml. The manifest is static: Gen Studio reads it without running any of your code. There are two kinds of step. A worker is a Python program of yours that Gen Studio starts and talks to. A comfyui step is a ComfyUI workflow template that runs on the managed ComfyUI.
A checkout of Gen Studio with uv sync done, so gen works. Python 3.12 or newer for a worker. An idea small enough for one step: one input, one output.

Scaffold it. The id is author.name, in lower case: gen new extension me.foley --kind worker --kind comfyui makes a template step instead. --stage names the stage (the default is the name part of the id) and --dir sets the parent folder (the default is where you are). A worker's environment is made at once, with its uv.lock. Look at what you got: me.foley/ gen-extension.toml the manifest quality.toml the quality checklist worker/ its own uv project (pyproject.toml, src/) tests/test_contract.py the worker speaks the protocol tests/test_golden.py a real run, for you to fill in Describe the step in gen-extension.toml. A stage has an id, an input, an output, a recipe per profile and its form fields: [[stages]] id = "foley" input = "text" output = "text" runtime = "worker" worker = "main" [stages.recipes.fast] expected_seconds = 10 values = {} [stages.fields.prompt] label = "Prompt" type = "longtext" help = "The sound to make, in a few words" The app draws the step's form from [stages.fields.<key>], and the core refuses values that don't fit. Field types are text, longtext, int, float, choice, bool, file and budget. Write the worker in worker/src/. It implements initialize and run and is served with gen_sdk.v1.worker.serve. In run, read the request from the job spec, write your files into params.output_dir, and return their paths. Report progress with ctx.progress, call ctx.check_cancelled() between chunks of work, and raise the typed errors (UserInputError for a bad request). Log to stderr: stdout belongs to the protocol. Pin what the step downloads. Each [[weights]] entry names a Hugging Face repo, a full 40-character revision and the file's sha256. The scaffold has a commented example. Fill in quality.toml and write the golden test: a real run that checks the output's structure (sizes, budgets), not its bytes. If the stage takes a prompt, add prompting.toml: the app's prompt guide for it (a summary, the structure, a placeholder, tips, what to avoid, about ten examples, sources). Check it: gen ext validate me.foley It checks the manifest, the pins, the environment, quality.toml and prompting.toml. Install it. Put the folder in extensions/ of the Gen Studio folder, or in extensions/ of the data folder, and restart the app. gen ext list shows it with its stages.

Where Add step offers it: a stage's requires says what must be up the path, for example ["rig"], ["image", "mesh|rig"] or ["after:turnaround"] (the step it follows). A ComfyUI step: the template is an API workflow JSON with whole-value {{name}} placeholders. Prefer ComfyUI's core nodes. The core pins each template by its sha256, and [scheduler] declares the graphics memory it needs. Another model for someone else's step: an add-on sets extends to the parent's id. It is on only while the parent is on, and may provide the parent's stages with another model. The step then gets a Model choice beside Profile. Where it sits in Settings: category groups it (image, 3d, motion, audio, voice, text, anime). Research code that isn't a package: a worker pins it with source (a git URL) and rev (a 40-character commit). Types: a worker type-checks with strict pyright in its own environment. An environment too heavy to install in CI ships stubs in typings/, or a reasoned [typecheck.skip] entry in quality.toml. Hooks and panels: an extension can also run a function when a step finishes or fails, and add a panel to the app. examples/extensions/me.queue-stats/ in the repository is a small one with both. Rules that keep extensions safe to share: workers get file paths, never bytes. Each worker keeps its own environment and depends only on gen-sdk. Every result must be reproducible from its meta.json. The full manifest and protocol are in the repository: AGENTS.md (the section on writing an extension) and docs/architecture.md. The shipped extensions in extensions/ are the best examples.
Turn extensions on and off Steps and fields: what the shipped stages declare. The extensions, one page each The gen command
